title: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models via Nearest Neighbor Calibration
abstract: Pre-trained language models (PLMs) have exhibited remarkable few-shot learning capabilities when provided a few examples in a natural language prompt as demonstrations of test instances, i.e., in-context learning. However, the performance of in-context learning is susceptible to the choice of prompt format, training examples and the ordering of the training examples. In this paper, we propose a novel nearest-neighbor calibration framework for in-context learning to ease this issue. It is inspired by a phenomenon that the in-context learning paradigm produces incorrect labels when inferring training instances, which provides a useful supervised signal to calibrate predictions. Thus, our method directly augments the predictions with a $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$NN) classifier over a datastore of cached few-shot instance representations obtained by PLMs and their corresponding labels. Then adaptive neighbor selection and feature regularization modules are introduced to make full use of a few support instances to reduce the $k$NN retrieval noise. Experiments on various few-shot text classification tasks demonstrate that our method significantly improves in-context learning, while even achieving comparable performance with state-of-the-art tuning-based approaches in some sentiment analysis tasks.

claims.text: In-context learning produces incorrect predictions when inferring the labels of few-shot training support instances themselves.
Nearest neighbor calibration (KNN-C) achieves a 12.8% absolute average accuracy improvement over standard in-context learning on single-sentence NLP tasks.
KNN-C achieves a 6.2% absolute average accuracy improvement over standard in-context learning on sentence-pair NLP tasks.
Combining Adaptive Neighbor Selection and Feature Regularization modules reduces retrieval noise in kNN-augmented in-context learning.
Standard in-context learning yields significantly smaller improvements on sentence-pair tasks compared to single-sentence tasks.

limitations.text: In-context learning performance is highly sensitive to the choice of prompting templates, verbalizers, training examples, and example ordering.
A substantial performance gap remains between KNN-C and fine-tuning based methods on sentence-pair tasks like text entailment and paraphrasing.
Optimizing the Adaptive Neighbor Selection and Feature Regularization modules on small datasets can result in instability and fail to find optimal solutions.

future_work.text: Combine the nearest neighbor calibration framework with larger pre-trained language models.
Investigate the potential reasons for the performance gap between nearest neighbor calibration and fine-tuning methods on sentence-pair tasks.
Explore nearest neighbor calibration on larger training datasets beyond the few-shot adaptation setting.

methodologies.name: Nearest Neighbor Calibration (KNN-C)
methodologies.description: An in-context learning framework that interpolates language model predictions with kNN retrieval over cached few-shot support instance hidden representations, enhanced with lightweight adaptive neighbor selection and feature regularization modules.
